-98.22150,26.18450.name: Reproductive Institute of South Texas
-98.22150,26.18450.desc: A fertility clinic reporting to the CDC's National ART Surveillance System. Medical director: Esteban O. Brown, MD. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. Reporting is required of every US clinic performing assisted reproduction, under the Fertility Clinic Success Rate and Certification Act, so this is close to a complete register rather than a list of members. What it records is cycles started, which is not the same as children born.

-71.23556,42.37624.name: Alkermes, Inc.
-71.23556,42.37624.desc: An organisation accredited by AAALAC International for its care and use of laboratory animals. Accreditation is voluntary and paid for, so this is a list of organisations that chose to be inspected rather than a register of everyone doing the work. An organisation absent from it is not accredited; that says nothing about whether it uses animals. In several countries the largest users are absent for exactly that reason. The directory gives a city and country and no street address, so this point marks where the organisation is registered rather than the building where animals are held.

-2.61487,51.47204.name: Bristol fertility clinic
-2.61487,51.47204.state: Spire Bristol Hospital-The Glen, Redland Hill, Bristol, BS6 6UT
-2.61487,51.47204.company: Satellite clinic to Bristol Centre for Reproductive Medicine
-2.61487,51.47204.desc: A fertility clinic licensed and inspected by the Human Fertilisation and Embryology Authority. Satellite clinic to Bristol Centre for Reproductive Medicine. A satellite is where patients are seen; the licence sits with the parent clinic, so the regulator's paperwork and the treatment are in different places. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. The HFEA licenses every clinic in the United Kingdom, inspects them, and publishes findings and success rates clinic by clinic. No other fertility regulator publishes at this level, which makes the UK the one country where this sector can be read rather than estimated.

-51.21220,-30.03902.desc: A centre accredited by REDLARA, the Latin American Network of Assisted Reproduction. Website: http://clinicaproser.com.br/. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. REDLARA accreditation is voluntary and its members report to a shared registry, which is why Latin America can be read at all — most countries in the region have no national register of clinics. What it is not is a complete list: a clinic outside REDLARA appears nowhere.

5.48758,52.55068.name: Wageningen Bioveterinary Research
5.48758,52.55068.state: Houtribweg 39, 8221 RA Lelystad, the Netherlands, Netherlands
5.48758,52.55068.desc: A BSL3+ laboratory, operational. Run by Wageningen University. It is categorised as a university laboratory, working on both human and animal health. There is no international register of laboratories at this containment level and no obligation to declare one, so this record comes from a research project rather than a regulator. What that project could not find out is absent here too.

-77.03200,38.88700.name: USDA NIFA — grant database
-77.03200,38.88700.state: Washington DC — USDA Waterfront Centre, 800 9th St SW
-77.03200,38.88700.desc: Every US agricultural research grant, searchable by recipient, amount and subject. Public funding shapes which crops and traits get studied long before any product exists, and this is where that can be traced without asking anyone.

-77.03200,38.88700.name: USDA National Organic Program
-77.03200,38.88700.state: Washington DC — USDA AMS, 1400 Independence Ave SW
-77.03200,38.88700.desc: Organic certification prohibits engineered organisms, which makes the organic standard the largest binding GMO restriction in American agriculture — not by law but by contract, and enforced through inspection rather than a regulator. When engineered pollen reaches an organic field the grower carries the loss, because the standard tests the product and does not ask who caused the presence.

-74.00800,40.71060.name: Pfizer — biologics and gene therapy
-74.00800,40.71060.desc: Runs gene-therapy programmes for haemophilia and Duchenne muscular dystrophy alongside its vaccine business, and manufactures viral vectors in-house. A company of this size entering gene therapy changes what the field costs to enter, because trial and manufacturing capacity stop being the limit.

-97.72500,30.39000.name: Natera
-97.72500,30.39000.desc: Sells non-invasive prenatal testing, reading fetal DNA from a pregnant woman’s blood. Millions of tests a year, and expansion into rare microdeletions where a positive result is more often wrong than right — a screening industry selling certainty about conditions it cannot reliably detect.

16.41300,48.23400.name: UN Security Council Resolution 1540 Committee
16.41300,48.23400.desc: Requires every state to prohibit non-state actors from acquiring biological, chemical and nuclear weapons, and to report on the measures it has taken. It is binding on all UN members, which is rare in this field — and its implementation is measured by self-reporting, so what it actually produces is a record of what governments say they have done.

-84.08330,9.93330.name: Sala Constitucional de Costa Rica — expediente 12-017013-0007-CO
-84.08330,9.93330.state: San José — Sala Constitucional de la Corte Suprema de Justicia
-84.08330,9.93330.desc: In September 2014 the constitutional chamber cancelled the permits granted for planting engineered maize in Costa Rica, ruling for the ecological organisations that had brought the action two years earlier. The route to that judgment is what makes it worth studying. When a Monsanto affiliate obtained permission in January 2013 to plant in Guanacaste, campaigners went to the municipalities rather than only to the courts: within about two years, 75 of the country's 81 cantons had declared themselves territories free of engineered crops, alongside statements against the maize from the governing bodies of all four public universities and from the agronomists' professional college. The legal argument that followed rested partly on municipal autonomy — a national permit to plant inside a canton that had prohibited it. A constitutional court is not usually reachable by a village council, and this is the clearest case on the map of local government being used as the route to one.
